content.title: LO8
content.description: This unit distinguishes pure substances from mixtures and compares solutions, colloids, and suspensions by composition, particle size, and behavior.

concepts.title: Pure substance
concepts.description: A pure substance has a fixed composition and characteristic properties; it consists of a single element or compound rather than a physical mixture.

concepts.title: Solution
concepts.description: A solution is a homogeneous mixture in which one or more solutes are evenly dispersed through a solvent.

concepts.title: Solute
concepts.description: A solute is a substance dissolved in a solution; its identity and amount help determine the solution's composition.

concepts.title: Solvent
concepts.description: A solvent is the medium that dissolves a solute and usually determines the physical state of the resulting solution.

concepts.title: Colloid
concepts.description: A colloid contains dispersed particles larger than those in a true solution but small enough to remain suspended without quickly settling.

concepts.title: Tyndall Effect
concepts.description: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloid particles, making a beam visible as it passes through a colloid.

concepts.title: Suspension
concepts.description: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture with particles large enough to settle over time and often be separated by filtration.

content.title: LO9
content.description: This unit compares material properties used to describe appearance and mechanical behavior, including texture, uniformity, strength, elasticity, bounce, and malleability.

concepts.title: Texture
concepts.description: Texture describes a material's surface and the size, shape, and arrangement of its visible particles or features.

concepts.title: Uniformity
concepts.description: Uniformity describes how consistently a material's composition and properties are distributed throughout a sample.

concepts.title: Strength
concepts.description: Strength is a material's ability to withstand an applied force without breaking or undergoing permanent deformation.

concepts.title: Elasticity
concepts.description: Elasticity is the ability of a material to return toward its original shape after a deforming force is removed.

concepts.title: Bounce
concepts.description: Bounce describes how well an object rebounds after impact, depending on its elasticity and how much energy is lost during the collision.

concepts.title: Malleability
concepts.description: Malleability is the ability of a solid material to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets without cracking.

content.title: LO10
content.description: This unit uses balanced chemical equations and quantitative relationships to calculate reactant and product amounts, including yields and limiting reagents.

concepts.title: Stoichiometry
concepts.description: Stoichiometry uses mole ratios from a balanced chemical equation to calculate the amounts of reactants consumed and products formed.

concepts.title: Mole
concepts.description: The mole is the SI unit for amount of substance and represents Avogadro's number of specified particles, such as atoms, molecules, or ions.

concepts.title: Molar mass
concepts.description: Molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance, usually expressed in grams per mole and calculated from its chemical formula.

concepts.title: Standard temperature and pressure (STP)
concepts.description: STP is a defined reference temperature and pressure used to compare gas properties; the exact reference values depend on the convention being used.

concepts.title: Dimensional analysis (unit conversions)
concepts.description: Dimensional analysis converts measurements by multiplying by ratios equal to one, arranged so unwanted units cancel and the desired unit remains.

concepts.title: Percentage yield
concepts.description: Percentage yield compares the amount of product actually obtained with the theoretical maximum, expressed as a percentage.

concepts.title: Limiting reagent
concepts.description: The limiting reagent is consumed first in a reaction and therefore determines the maximum amount of product that can form.

content.title: LO11
content.description: This unit classifies chemical reactions by how reactants rearrange into products and uses common reaction patterns to interpret chemical change.

concepts.title: Synthesis reaction
concepts.description: A synthesis reaction combines two or more reactants to form a single product, often represented as A + B → AB.

concepts.title: Decomposition reaction
concepts.description: A decomposition reaction breaks one compound into two or more simpler products, often requiring energy to initiate the change.

concepts.title: Single-replacement reaction
concepts.description: In a single-replacement reaction, a free element replaces another element in a compound when the reaction is chemically favorable.

concepts.title: Double-replacement reaction
concepts.description: A double-replacement reaction exchanges ions between two compounds and may produce a precipitate, gas, or molecular substance such as water.

content.title: LO12
content.description: This unit explores molecular polarity, intermolecular attractions, electronegativity, and molecular shape to explain how structure influences substance properties.

concepts.title: Intermolecular forces
concepts.description: Intermolecular forces are attractions between particles that influence physical properties such as boiling point, melting point, viscosity, and solubility.

concepts.title: London dispersion force
concepts.description: London dispersion forces arise from temporary fluctuations in electron distribution and occur between all atoms and molecules.

concepts.title: Dipole-dipole force
concepts.description: Dipole-dipole forces are attractions between the partial positive and partial negative ends of neighboring polar molecules.

concepts.title: Electronegativity
concepts.description: Electronegativity measures how strongly an atom attracts shared electrons in a chemical bond and helps predict bond polarity.

concepts.title: Polarity
concepts.description: Polarity is an uneven distribution of electrical charge in a bond or molecule, determined by electronegativity differences and molecular geometry.

concepts.title: VESPR theory
concepts.description: VSEPR theory predicts molecular shape by considering repulsion between regions of electron density around a central atom.

content.title: LO13
content.description: This unit introduces metals and redox chemistry, focusing on electron transfer and how oxidation and reduction occur together in reactions.

concepts.title: Metals
concepts.description: Metals are elements that typically conduct heat and electricity, are malleable and ductile, and form positive ions by losing electrons.

concepts.title: Oxidation-reduction (redox) reaction
concepts.description: A redox reaction involves electron transfer: one species is oxidized as another is reduced, with oxidation numbers changing accordingly.

concepts.title: Oxidation
concepts.description: Oxidation is the loss of electrons by a species and corresponds to an increase in its oxidation number.

concepts.title: Reduction
concepts.description: Reduction is the gain of electrons by a species and corresponds to a decrease in its oxidation number.

content.title: LO14
content.description: This unit examines electrochemical cells and redox processes by separating electron-transfer steps and identifying species unchanged by the reaction.

concepts.title: Oxidation-reduction (redox) reaction
concepts.description: Redox reactions couple oxidation and reduction; tracking electron transfer and oxidation numbers helps explain how electrochemical cells operate.

concepts.title: Half-reactions
concepts.description: Half-reactions show oxidation and reduction separately, including the electrons gained or lost so the overall electron transfer can be balanced.

concepts.title: Electrochemical cell
concepts.description: An electrochemical cell uses a redox reaction to transfer electrons through a circuit or uses electrical energy to drive a chemical reaction.

concepts.title: Galvanic cell
concepts.description: A galvanic cell converts energy from a spontaneous redox reaction into electrical energy as electrons flow through an external circuit.

concepts.title: Spectator ions
concepts.description: Spectator ions are present in solution but remain unchanged during a reaction, so they are omitted from the net ionic equation.

content.title: LO15
content.description: This unit connects thermodynamics with reaction kinetics through energy, heat, work, enthalpy, entropy, spontaneity, and the role of catalysts.

concepts.title: System
concepts.description: A system is the portion of matter or space selected for study; everything outside it is considered the surroundings.

concepts.title: Thermodynamic
concepts.description: Thermodynamics describes relationships among heat, work, and energy, and how energy changes in a system and its surroundings.

concepts.title: Kinetics
concepts.description: Chemical kinetics studies reaction rates and how factors such as concentration, temperature, surface area, and catalysts affect them.

concepts.title: Energy
concepts.description: Energy is the capacity to transfer heat or perform work and can change form while remaining conserved in a complete system.

concepts.title: Heat
concepts.description: Heat is energy transferred between objects or systems because of a temperature difference, flowing spontaneously from warmer to cooler regions.

concepts.title: Maximum work
concepts.description: Maximum work is the greatest useful work a system can deliver under specified conditions, reached in an ideal reversible process.

concepts.title: Law of conservation of energy
concepts.description: The law of conservation of energy states that energy is not created or destroyed, but transferred or transformed between forms.

concepts.title: Endothermic
concepts.description: An endothermic process absorbs heat from its surroundings; at constant pressure, its enthalpy change is positive.

concepts.title: Exothermic
concepts.description: An exothermic process releases heat to its surroundings; at constant pressure, its enthalpy change is negative.

concepts.title: Heat content
concepts.description: Heat content commonly refers to enthalpy, a state function whose change equals heat transferred at constant pressure when only pressure-volume work occurs.

concepts.title: Enthalpy change
concepts.description: Enthalpy change is the difference between the products' and reactants' enthalpies and indicates heat absorbed or released at constant pressure.

concepts.title: Energy diagram
concepts.description: An energy diagram plots the energy of reactants and products along reaction progress, showing the activation barrier and overall energy change.

concepts.title: Activation energy
concepts.description: Activation energy is the energy barrier reactants must overcome to reach the transition state and proceed toward products.

concepts.title: Activated complex
concepts.description: The activated complex, or transition state, is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement formed near the top of the reaction energy barrier.

concepts.title: Entropy(S)
concepts.description: Entropy describes the dispersal of energy and the number of microscopic arrangements available to a system.

concepts.title: Spontaneity
concepts.description: Spontaneity describes whether a process is thermodynamically favored under specified conditions; it does not indicate how fast the process occurs.

concepts.title: Gibbs free energy
concepts.description: Gibbs free energy combines enthalpy and entropy; at constant temperature and pressure, a negative change indicates a spontaneous process.

concepts.title: Catalyst
concepts.description: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy and is regenerated, without changing the equilibrium position.

content.title: LO16
content.description: This unit models gases using particle motion and gas laws, relating pressure, volume, temperature, and amount under defined conditions.

concepts.title: Gas
concepts.description: A gas has no fixed shape or volume; its particles move freely, spread to fill a container, and can be compressed.

concepts.title: Natural law
concepts.description: A natural law summarizes a consistent relationship observed in nature; gas laws express quantitative relationships among gas variables.

concepts.title: Pressure
concepts.description: Gas pressure results from particles colliding with the walls of their container and is measured as force per unit area.

concepts.title: Atmosphere
concepts.description: The atmosphere is the mixture of gases surrounding Earth; its weight exerts atmospheric pressure on surfaces and fluids.

concepts.title: Barometers
concepts.description: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, traditionally by balancing air pressure against a column of liquid or through a sealed sensor.

concepts.title: Boyle's Law
concepts.description: Boyle's law states that a gas's pressure varies inversely with its volume when temperature and amount of gas remain constant.

concepts.title: Charles's Law
concepts.description: Charles's law states that a gas's volume varies directly with its absolute temperature when pressure and amount of gas remain constant.

concepts.title: Absolute Zero
concepts.description: Absolute zero is 0 kelvin, the lower limit of the thermodynamic temperature scale and the point of minimum thermal energy.

concepts.title: Kinetic Theory of Matter
concepts.description: The kinetic theory models matter as particles in constant motion; for an ideal gas, average particle kinetic energy is proportional to absolute temperature.

concepts.title: Idea Gas
concepts.description: The ideal-gas model assumes particles have negligible volume, move randomly, and undergo elastic collisions; it approximates real gases best at low pressure and high temperature.

content.title: LO17
content.description: This unit explains how gas particles spread through space or pass through tiny openings and how their relative rates depend on molar mass.

concepts.title: Diffusion
concepts.description: Diffusion is the net spreading of particles from regions of higher concentration to lower concentration through random motion.

concepts.title: Effusion
concepts.description: Effusion is the escape of gas particles through a tiny opening into a region of lower pressure.

concepts.title: Graham's Law of Effusion
concepts.description: Graham's law states that, under the same conditions, gas effusion rates are inversely proportional to the square roots of their molar masses.
